title: Japan 12th in Global Innovation Ranking
paragraphs: Japan has been ranked 12th in this year's Global Innovation Index, keeping the same position it held last year.

The index is published every year by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), a United Nations agency. It compares 139 economies using about 80 different measures, such as research spending, patents and education.

Switzerland took first place for the 16th year in a row, followed by Sweden and the United States. South Korea came fourth, making it the highest-ranked economy in the Asia-Pacific region, while Singapore was fifth and China was tenth. Japan, South Korea and China all stayed in the same positions as the previous year.

Japan performed very well in some areas. It ranked first in the world for the complexity of the goods it produces and exports, and third for both patent families and research and development carried out by businesses. The report praised the depth of research led by Japanese companies and their close connections with universities. In addition, the Tokyo-Yokohama area was ranked as the world's second-largest innovation cluster, after the Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou region in China.

However, Japan was weaker in other areas, including higher education, the number of science and engineering graduates, and jobs that require advanced knowledge. The report also noted that Japan's shrinking youth population is affecting its performance.

The result leaves Japan well behind its own goal, and some way behind its Asian neighbors. Under its 2025 intellectual property strategy, the Japanese government aims to reach fourth place or higher in the index by 2035.

The report also looked at wider global trends in innovation. It found that spending on research and development around the world grew by 3.3% in 2025, and it is expected to rise by 3.6% in 2026, reaching $3.4 trillion.
